library.description: Browser backend plugins for localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and native IndexedDB, with optional reactive queries.

blocks.text: 为 `localStorage`、`sessionStorage`、Cookie 和 IndexedDB 提供浏览器后端。把选定后端安装到 `@migaia/storage-host`，由宿主负责准备与释放。

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/storage-web @migaia/storage-host @migaia/storage-contract

blocks.text: 示例需要支持顶层 `await` 的浏览器 ESM 环境，以及所选后端对应的原生浏览器 API。
输出 `dark`。释放宿主会关闭其拥有的监听器与连接，不清空浏览器持久化数据。

rows: 文本与同步读写，仅 JS 可见 Cookie
文本、字节、记录、原生事务、索引

blocks.text: 各后端入口还导出不透明种类标识及精确的选项、存储类型。`plugins/*` 入口导出对应插件函数。第一个参数为原生选项，第二个可选参数为 Feature 记录。共享能力与上下文类型直接从 `@migaia/storage-contract` 导入。
内存后端、`createStorageHost`、`defineFeature` 与后端作者接口属于 `@migaia/storage-host`。实体仓储、结构适配与存储编解码器属于 `@migaia/storage-host/entity`。
实体唯一约束写入需要真实 record 事务或后端原生原子 value 提交端点；内置浏览器后端均提供。自定义纯 value 后端未登记 `core.registerValueCommit` 时，唯一写入在 schema 执行和修改前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`，普通 KV 不受影响。作者契约见 host 实体使用指南。

`store.use(kv)` 提供 `getMany`、`setMany`、`removeMany` 与 `removeByPrefix`。IndexedDB 批量在同一个原生事务中执行，支持字符串、数字、日期、字节和元组键；字符串仍与原单键方法共享数据。读取结果保留输入顺序与重复位置，缺失项为 `undefined`，删除返回实际数量；写批中的规范重复键在 I/O 前报 `INVALID_ARGUMENT`。空批不进入管线或原生事务。

localStorage、sessionStorage 与 Cookie 可批量读取；多键写需要 WAL，未配置时在修改前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。默认 namespace codec 保留字符串的 `sw1` 格式，结构键使用独立 `sw2` 格式；`keys()` 仍只列字符串，命名空间清理覆盖两种格式。自定义 codec 需成对提供 `encodeStorageKey` 与 `decodeStorageKey` 才能读取非字符串批量键，缺少时在原生 I/O 前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。
三个数据通道共用一个原生读写事务。只有通过所提供 scope 发起的方法参与事务。完成等待真实原生终态，失败回滚该事务。回调内不要等待定时器、网络请求或独立的根写入。原生事务失活时以 `TRANSACTION_FAILED` 失败，并保留原生原因；守护请求不会重新进入业务回调。
可选的 `features/reactive` 入口为受支持查询链增加 `.live()`。每个已安装 Feature 拥有独立服务，首次使用时才接入来源。响应式 Runtime 由调用者拥有。
浏览器来源保留最终可见性边界：本地存储为 `document-eventual`，会话存储为 `top-level-context-eventual`，Cookie 为 `origin-js-visible-eventual`，IndexedDB 为 `origin-eventual`。四者保留原有 1000 毫秒协调轮询。变化仅表示查询失效，不承诺复制或立即观察任意原始写入。

items: 文本方法接受字符串键与字符串值；不存在的文本返回 `null`，记录返回 `undefined`。
`clearValues` 只清文本通道，`clearAll` 只清该后端拥有的通道与命名空间。
同键跨通道写入报 `DUPLICATE_KEY`；显式 `conflictPolicy: 'replace'` 才在原子操作中替换其他通道。
Cookie scope 在安装时固定。HttpOnly Cookie 不可见，`has: false` 不证明其不存在。
释放先封闭新接纳，再排空已接纳工作。显式清理通过返回的 Promise 传播失败，原始原因链保留。
宿主开始安装后的失败以 `@migaia/storage-host` 的 `BACKEND_INSTALL_FAILED` 拒绝，原浏览器错误保留在原因链。
按 `(source, code)` 分支。浏览器错误来源为 `@migaia/storage-web`，共享并发、取消与所有权错误保留原包身份。

blocks.text: 选项、原生活跃窗口与生命周期详见使用指南。

IndexedDB 通过 `store.watch(key, ctx?)` 提供原生文本失效迭代器。仅当实例已准入当前 realm 的 IndexedDB 与 BroadcastChannel 时 `capabilities.changeFeed` 为 `true`；未准入时调用报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。提示携带原宿主的组织 UUID，收到提示后重新读取已提交的原生值；这不提供历史重放或每次写入一条事件的保证。迭代器复用原资源清理，使用后调用 `dispose()`。

IndexedDB 原生提供 `ttl`：`store.use(ttl)` 的 `expire`、`remaining`、`persist` 支持文本、字节和记录目标，事务内用 `scope.use(ttl)`。`setMany` 的 `ttlMs` 与值在同一个原生事务提交或回滚。缺省不设期限，到期的点读、枚举和索引查询视为缺失，并在原事务中惰性删除、更新修订与变更提示；不启动清理定时器。期限按安装时捕获的本地时钟锚点与原 scheduler 推进，使用缺省时钟时跨页面和重开保持可比较。IndexedDB 没有向量通道，向量 TTL 目标在 I/O 前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。

文本组织视图的宿主缺省组织使用配置 namespace，其它组织使用 namespace + "/" + orgId，继续复用捕获的原生客户端、namespace codec 与 Cookie scope。配置目标以 "/" 加规范 UUID 结尾时在原生 I/O 前拒绝，单独 UUID 合法。dropOrg 只清该目标，保留其它组织及插件前缀，既有视图仍可复用；借用实体保留原生原子唯一写入端点。IndexedDB 使用相同规则映射 dbName；dropOrg 先让目标连接进入原生 close-pending 并排空其事务，再等待该目标的 deleteDatabase 完成。删除期间新打开等待同一原生请求；完成后原视图可重新打开。其它实例沿原 versionchange 关闭；拒绝关闭的外部连接会使原生删除继续等待，宿主不会提前恢复打开并让迟到删除损坏新数据。

localStorage 仅在成功捕获同一 Window 的真实 localStorage 与 storage 事件源后声明 changeFeed:true；单独注入 Storage-like 仍为 false。原 watch/subscribeChanges 同时接本实例已提交写与跨文档原生事件，按 storageArea、namespace codec 和组织过滤；宿主关闭释放原监听者。通知由接收方原 controller 编号，不含原生写入方历史序号；应重读当前值，不保证逐写投递或同页面其它独立实例的原生事件。组织视图保留 watch 方法，调用仍检查运行时能力，且不获得后端关闭权。

sections.heading: 原生 Blob 与 File 存储

blocks.text: 从专用子入口选择 `indexedDbBlobFeature`，得到 `store.api.blobs` 与 `scope.api.blobs`。Blob/File 使用原生结构化克隆；File 的名称、类型和最后修改时间在重开后保留。仓库默认 `__migaia_blobs__`，可用 `{ storeName }` 指定；声明碰撞在开库前拒绝。Blob 请求与 records 共用原事务、取消、配额归一和回滚；组织视图使用自己的真实数据库及原事务拥有者。Feature 不授予关闭数据库的方法。

IndexedDB 支持从 `@migaia/storage-host/journal` 调用 `storageLogStore(hostOrOrg, 'indexed-db', { prefix })`。私有行使用既有 META 对象仓库内的数组键命名空间。业务 `clearAll` 保留历史；删除组织使旧日志句柄失效，原业务视图仍可重新打开。缓存模式下，重新打开同一物理组织和前缀前须释放原日志。head、state 与记录随原生事务一同提交，缓存索引在真实 complete 事件内发布。

有原生 Web Locks 时，原资源期间独占与缓存路径保持，冲突打开报 LOCK_REJECTED。缺少 Web Locks、又未声明实际私有 factory 时，原 namespace 声明 `indexExclusive:false`：storageLogStore 不再拒绝，而是在每个操作的原 journal-store readwrite 事务内恢复/读取最新 lastSeq、state 与记录，不跨操作保留索引。注入 factory 有 Web Locks 时同样使用原缓存路径；`journalFactoryIsPrivate:true` 仅适用于数据宇宙局限当前 realm 且不转发共享持久库的真实私有 factory，继续复用原逻辑锁与缓存拥有者。对象身份本身不证明隔离。此命名空间支持本身不启用全局自动捕获或显式选择的 undo。

sections.heading: IndexedDB 全局日志与显式 undo

blocks.text: 在 Host 的 `journal` 初始化函数中，用当前组织的 `storageLogStore` 打开原生 binlog 与 undo 仓库，再将同一对象交给 logger 插件及 `atomicBinlog` / `atomicUndo`。选择带 undo 插件的 logger 时必须显式设置 `indexedDbUndo: true`；缺省或 false 在业务原生事务前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。通过 Host 配置得到的后端与组织视图可调用 `undo(txId)`，恢复由原事务 builder 执行。

文本、字节、记录、清空与绝对 TTL 元数据的实际写入顺序保留在同一原生事务中；重复写入不按通道重排。原生 complete 才发布日志索引，回滚不增加日志序列。首次组织只读同样完成该组织的一次配置；惰性过期删除与日志一起提交。所有契约写入维护原生点修订，删除或清空后保留墓碑，因此其它无日志契约句柄的 clear/recreate 也会使旧 undo 报 `UNDO_CONFLICT`，在恢复任何目标前拒绝。undo 比对原物理镜像，恢复原绝对期限，不延长过期时间。

原生 Feature 直接借用 IDBDatabase / IDBTransaction，超出当前文本、字节、记录镜像域。启用提交日志的组合在交出该原生句柄前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`；普通与仅遥测配置下的 Blob / 自定义原生 Feature 保持可用。此有限组合仍待共享目标与 codec 方案复查。严格 IndexedDB 不声明允许最终镜像后等待外部 WAL 的能力，该组合在业务 I/O 前拒绝。

localStorage/sessionStorage/Cookie 可用 `redo: true` 显式启用文本事务与多键写，并同时选择 `journal.redoWal: logger.wal`。该组合要求真实 Web Locks；所有参与者借用同一个真实、可见最新 pending 的原 WAL 对象。仅目标同名或不同 memoryLogStore 不构成共享。浏览器同源 popup 可直接借用 opener 持有的精确 Logger/WAL；持久恢复可用另一个 IDB 后端的 storageLogStore 作为单拥有者载体，不能用待增强文本后端给自己承载 WAL。

原 transaction owner 管理 text-only scope，读取自身 draft；先完整编码，再 wal.begin，顺序应用、binlog、complete，之后发布一次失效提示和成功。应用或 complete 失败会停止该实例准入并保留 pending，重开或已打开的参与 peer 在物理保护内先恢复再读取。回调失败不应用 draft。未选 redo 时原标量与同步行为保持；选中异步 journal 后同步入口沿原 ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY 拒绝。redo 不宣称原生原子提交；undo/atomicBinlog/atomicUndo 与 raw 原生 Feature 句柄在该组合中修改前拒绝。独立 WAL 缓存之间的自动跨页恢复不作保证。
同一实例的 draft 活跃时，该实例根入口的读取、写入与另一事务立即报 `WRITE_CONFLICT`；独立调用方显式指定 `ConcurrencyPolicy.wait()` 也不会排队。回调内使用已提供的 scope。该隔离避免回调重入等待自身持有的 Web Lock；同实例排队 wait 尚未兑现。其它实例仍沿原 Web Locks 等待或取消，未选 redo 的原有行为保持。

Cookie 的 `redo: true` 复用同一原事务/WAL 协议；普通和 redo 写入共用原 cookie 编码、4096-byte 校验、固定 scope 与可见性检查。批量读取仍由同一原解析器读取一次可见 header，再合入当前 draft。redo 模式把 maxAge 在准备时转换为绝对 expiresAt 镜像，重放不续期；超过原生 Date 域的 maxAge 只在该新组合修改前拒绝，普通 Cookie maxAge 域和 Max-Age 优先级不变。该模式仅记录 JS 可见 cookie，HttpOnly/未知 scope 的原限制保持。

普通 localStorage、sessionStorage 与 Cookie 声明 `capabilities.batch: false`；IndexedDB 与显式 redo/WAL 组合声明为 true。启用 commit journal 时不提供原生 IndexedDB 句柄，错误 source 为 `@migaia/storage-contract`、code 为 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。IndexedDB 不提供向量引擎。本仓库网站在新 host 包发布前继续使用已发布的 storage-web 0.0.8。

sections.id: 实体编解码器与复制边界
sections.heading: 实体编解码器与复制边界

blocks.text: 实体编解码器从 `@migaia/storage-host/entity` 导入。`jsonCodec` 的 `output` 为 `text`，使用严格的可移植 JSON；`structuredCodec` 的 `output` 为 `structured`，把结构化值交给后端；`binaryCodec` 的 `output` 为 `binary`，处理 `Uint8Array`。`selectCodec` 根据后端能力决定直连、回退或拒绝。

`jsonCodec` 不接受超出可移植值范围的对象，也不能表示循环。需要保留 `Map` 与 `Set` 时，使用 `@migaia/serialize/codecs/collections-json` 的 `defineCollectionsJsonCodec`，再由 `@migaia/storage-host/authoring/codec` 的 `fromValueCodec` 适配。`structuredCodec` 可交给后端保存可 structured-clone 的内建类型与循环。
`structuredCodec` 的 `encode/decode` 原样返回值，不复制；真正复制在记录后端。IndexedDB 的字节与记录写入遵循原生结构化克隆；内存后端会复制字节，记录采用 `structuredClone`。`binaryCodec` 校验后原样返回字节视图，后端负责写入快照。它们不重建 class 业务实例，也不做 schema 校验。
`schema` 处理领域表示，`codec` 处理保存格式。读取依次执行 `codec.decode`、版本迁移（存储表示）、`schema.decode`、`validate`。结构化输出在文本后端以 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` 拒绝，不会悄悄改成 JSON。
使用选定的浏览器插件与真实宿主。示例需要原生浏览器 API；注入端口不会让 Node 进程拥有浏览器能力。
安装在发布存储前完成准备。可复用插件定义创建独立安装，不要分享已由其他宿主拥有的存储。同种后端安装多次时使用不同 ID。重复释放共享完成 Promise，关闭后的存储不能复活。

rows: `local` 或 `session`；选择宿主中的注册项

blocks.text: 注入的 Storage 端口须实现 `length`、`getItem`、`setItem`、`removeItem`、`key`、`clear`。安装时探测可用性并保留已有数据。宿主拒绝访问报 `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`，配置非法报 `INVALID_CONFIG`，原生配额失败报 `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`。能力中的 5 MiB 为估计值，不保证浏览器实际配额。
默认命名空间 codec 使用 UTF-8 长度前缀，例如 `sw1:3:app:theme`，解码跳过损坏或其他空间的条目。自定义 codec 自行负责避免碰撞与格式迁移。`clearValues` 先快照匹配物理键再删除；原生失败可能留下部分清理结果，并保留失败的键。
`namespace` 默认 `default`，`document` 默认 `globalThis.document`。scope 默认 `{ path: '/' }`，所有写入与删除固定复用。domain 提供时须非空且不含空白或分号。`sameSite: 'none'`、`partitioned: true` 要求 `secure: true`。
写选项接受有效的 `expires: Date` 或整数 `maxAge`，已到期写入删除 Cookie。4096 字节上限覆盖包括属性的完整赋值。同名 Cookie 在多个 scope 同时可见时报 `COOKIE_SCOPE_AMBIGUOUS`，普通写入后不可见时报 `WRITE_FAILED`。JS 无法观察 HttpOnly 条目，也不能保证删除服务端 Cookie。

sections.heading: 批量 KV 与结构键

blocks.text: 通过 `store.use(kv)` 调用 `getMany(keys)`、`setMany(entries)`、`removeMany(keys)` 和 `removeByPrefix(prefix)`。IndexedDB 的每次非空批量调用只进入一次管线并使用一个原生事务；中途通道冲突使整批回滚。`getMany` 保留重复位置与缺失的 `undefined`；`removeMany` 对规范等价键只计一次。`setMany` 的重复规范键在任何 I/O 前报 `INVALID_ARGUMENT`；携带 `ttlMs` 还要求后端声明 TTL 能力。空批直接返回，不触发管线、hooks 或原生请求。
文本 Web 后端使用同步原生读取处理 `getMany`，Cookie 从一次可见 header 快照读取整批。未配置 WAL 时，多键写入和前缀删除在修改前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`，不能依靠逐个公开 `set` 组成原子批量。

默认 namespace codec 保留原字符串 `sw1` 格式；非字符串批量键以顶层 `sw2` 格式区分，键内容复用共享规范编码。任意旧字符串键均不会与结构键碰撞。`keys()` 保持 `string[]`，命名空间 clear 同时删除该命名空间的两种布局。自定义 `INamespaceCodec` 可以增加 `encodeStorageKey(namespace,key)` 与 `decodeStorageKey(namespace,physicalKey)`；两者必须成对提供并保证跨键类型不碰撞。缺少这两个接点时，新的非字符串批量读取在任何原生 I/O 前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`，原字符串布局和调用保持。

`dbName` 默认 `storage-web`；`kvStoreName`、`bytesStoreName`、`recordsStoreName` 默认分别为 `kv`、`bytes`、`records`。名称须非空、互异，并避开内部保留 store。`factory`、`keyRange` 默认 `globalThis.indexedDB`、`globalThis.IDBKeyRange`。可选 `owner.label` 仅为诊断元数据，不作为锁身份。
宿主在发布前打开并准备选定数据库，缺少内部 store 时以原生版本升级创建。`onversionchange` 关闭旧连接，打开被阻塞时拒绝，不发布未完成准备的后端。`cleanupLegacyRecords` 默认 `false`，启用后仅在迁移成功后删除历史 store。
事务 scope 将文本、字节、记录与索引维护放在同一个原生事务中。`scope.use(kv)` 提供结构键批量方法，`scope.use(records)` 提供查询与有界前缀删除。根文本键仍为字符串。记录与 scope 文本键遵循 `@migaia/storage-contract` 的 `IStorageKey`，支持 number、Date、ArrayBuffer 与嵌套数组。
回调内只等待原生操作和保留活跃性的微任务。定时器或网络等待可能结束原生活跃窗口，之后的方法以 `TRANSACTION_FAILED` 及原生原因失败；捕获方法失败不会让事务转为提交。回调关闭后 scope 方法失去准入，finalizer 使用同事务的独立真实视图。已接纳操作、迭代器、回调与 finalizer 全部排空后才释放资源。
`setBytes` 快照输入字节，记录写入使用结构化克隆，不支持的值报 `SERIALIZE_FAILED`。原生提交完成后才发布通知，监听器失败会被报告，不撤销已提交写入。
从 `@migaia/storage-host/entity` 导入中立仓储定义，并连接实际已安装的 IndexedDB 存储。

宿主实体模块负责结构检查、版本 envelope、迁移与投影。普通读取只物化声明版本，不自动写回；显式 `migrate()` 才持久化升级。原生二级索引 readiness 在实际当前事务快照中检查。 唯一约束写入需要真实 record 事务，或后端在安装期间通过 `core.registerValueCommit` 登记的原生原子 value 提交端点；内置浏览器后端均提供相应路径。自定义纯 value 后端缺少该端点时，唯一约束的 `put` 与 `migrate` 在 schema 执行和任何修改前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`；普通 KV 仍可使用。仅提供 `sync` 投影不构成跨页面原子性。
使用下例时显式安装 `@migaia/reactive`，Feature 放在后端插件第二参数。

`ready` 观察初始工作，`refresh()` 加入当前工作或请求新一代，`state` 为只读 computed。`keepPreviousData` 默认 `true`，`equals` 默认不抑制更新。可选 `scope`、`matches` 过滤失效提示，谓词失败会报告并保守刷新。`timeoutMs` 对每一代生效，`signal` 取消查询整个生命周期。清理后调用者的 Runtime 仍可用。
来源保留原生最终可见性。local、session、Cookie、IndexedDB 使用混合失效与 1000 毫秒协调；来自 `@migaia/storage-host` 的内存后端使用实例内 push，不轮询。来源不承诺立即观察任意外部写入。

同时检查 `source` 与 `code`。宿主开始安装后的失败以 host 的 `BACKEND_INSTALL_FAILED` 拒绝，原因链仍可达原浏览器错误。浏览器原生失败保留 cause 与 stack，并带有编码后的 `StorageError`；共享取消、锁、所有权检查、结构及编解码器错误保留原包身份。`ABORTED` 保留原取消原因。根据契约中的 `ConcurrencyPolicy` 处理并发，不因已提交通知失败重试业务写入。
`host.dispose()` 封闭新准入、取消排队成员、排空已接纳工作，再释放监听器与连接。显式后端清理以 `BACKEND_DISPOSE_FAILED` 传播失败，原始错误可达。重复显式调用共享 Promise，异步释放符号通过同一次清理提供独立的只报告完成投影。失败不会让已关闭后端复活。
用四个后端插件代替直接工厂，通过 `@migaia/storage-host` 安装。内存与宿主原语从该包导入，实体、结构适配与存储编解码器从其 `entity` 入口导入。旧响应式包装与宿主实时查询调用改为显式 `reactiveFeature(targetKind)` 和 `query.live()`。不提供历史工厂别名。

IndexedDB 通过 `store.watch(key, ctx?)` 提供原生文本失效迭代器。仅当实例已准入当前 realm 的 IndexedDB 与 BroadcastChannel 时 `capabilities.changeFeed` 为 `true`；未准入时调用报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。提示携带原宿主的组织 UUID，收到提示后重新读取已提交的原生值；这不提供历史重放或每次写入一条事件的保证。迭代器复用原资源清理，使用后调用 `dispose()`。

IndexedDB 原生提供 `ttl`：`store.use(ttl)` 的 `expire`、`remaining`、`persist` 支持文本、字节和记录目标，事务内用 `scope.use(ttl)`。`setMany` 的 `ttlMs` 与值在同一个原生事务提交或回滚。缺省不设期限，到期的点读、枚举和索引查询视为缺失，并在原事务中惰性删除、更新修订与变更提示；不启动清理定时器。期限按安装时捕获的本地时钟锚点与原 scheduler 推进，使用缺省时钟时跨页面和重开保持可比较。IndexedDB 没有向量通道，向量 TTL 目标在 I/O 前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。

文本组织视图的宿主缺省组织使用配置 namespace，其它组织使用 namespace + "/" + orgId，继续复用捕获的原生客户端、namespace codec 与 Cookie scope。配置目标以 "/" 加规范 UUID 结尾时在原生 I/O 前拒绝，单独 UUID 合法。dropOrg 只清该目标，保留其它组织及插件前缀，既有视图仍可复用；借用实体保留原生原子唯一写入端点。IndexedDB 使用相同规则映射 dbName；dropOrg 先让目标连接进入原生 close-pending 并排空其事务，再等待该目标的 deleteDatabase 完成。删除期间新打开等待同一原生请求；完成后原视图可重新打开。其它实例沿原 versionchange 关闭；拒绝关闭的外部连接会使原生删除继续等待，宿主不会提前恢复打开并让迟到删除损坏新数据。

localStorage 仅在成功捕获同一 Window 的真实 localStorage 与 storage 事件源后声明 changeFeed:true；单独注入 Storage-like 仍为 false。原 watch/subscribeChanges 同时接本实例已提交写与跨文档原生事件，按 storageArea、namespace codec 和组织过滤；宿主关闭释放原监听者。通知由接收方原 controller 编号，不含原生写入方历史序号；应重读当前值，不保证逐写投递或同页面其它独立实例的原生事件。组织视图保留 watch 方法，调用仍检查运行时能力，且不获得后端关闭权。

sections.heading: 原生 Blob 与 File 存储

blocks.text: 从专用子入口选择 `indexedDbBlobFeature`，得到 `store.api.blobs` 与 `scope.api.blobs`。Blob/File 使用原生结构化克隆；File 的名称、类型和最后修改时间在重开后保留。仓库默认 `__migaia_blobs__`，可用 `{ storeName }` 指定；声明碰撞在开库前拒绝。Blob 请求与 records 共用原事务、取消、配额归一和回滚；组织视图使用自己的真实数据库及原事务拥有者。Feature 不授予关闭数据库的方法。

IndexedDB 支持从 `@migaia/storage-host/journal` 调用 `storageLogStore(hostOrOrg, 'indexed-db', { prefix })`。私有行使用既有 META 对象仓库内的数组键命名空间。业务 `clearAll` 保留历史；删除组织使旧日志句柄失效，原业务视图仍可重新打开。缓存模式下，重新打开同一物理组织和前缀前须释放原日志。head、state 与记录随原生事务一同提交，缓存索引在真实 complete 事件内发布。

有原生 Web Locks 时，原资源期间独占与缓存路径保持，冲突打开报 LOCK_REJECTED。缺少 Web Locks、又未声明实际私有 factory 时，原 namespace 声明 `indexExclusive:false`：storageLogStore 不再拒绝，而是在每个操作的原 journal-store readwrite 事务内恢复/读取最新 lastSeq、state 与记录，不跨操作保留索引。注入 factory 有 Web Locks 时同样使用原缓存路径；`journalFactoryIsPrivate:true` 仅适用于数据宇宙局限当前 realm 且不转发共享持久库的真实私有 factory，继续复用原逻辑锁与缓存拥有者。对象身份本身不证明隔离。此命名空间支持本身不启用全局自动捕获或显式选择的 undo。

sections.heading: IndexedDB 全局日志与显式 undo

blocks.text: 在 Host 的 `journal` 初始化函数中，用当前组织的 `storageLogStore` 打开原生 binlog 与 undo 仓库，再将同一对象交给 logger 插件及 `atomicBinlog` / `atomicUndo`。选择带 undo 插件的 logger 时必须显式设置 `indexedDbUndo: true`；缺省或 false 在业务原生事务前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。通过 Host 配置得到的后端与组织视图可调用 `undo(txId)`，恢复由原事务 builder 执行。

文本、字节、记录、清空与绝对 TTL 元数据的实际写入顺序保留在同一原生事务中；重复写入不按通道重排。原生 complete 才发布日志索引，回滚不增加日志序列。首次组织只读同样完成该组织的一次配置；惰性过期删除与日志一起提交。所有契约写入维护原生点修订，删除或清空后保留墓碑，因此其它无日志契约句柄的 clear/recreate 也会使旧 undo 报 `UNDO_CONFLICT`，在恢复任何目标前拒绝。undo 比对原物理镜像，恢复原绝对期限，不延长过期时间。

原生 Feature 直接借用 IDBDatabase / IDBTransaction，超出当前文本、字节、记录镜像域。启用提交日志的组合在交出该原生句柄前报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`；普通与仅遥测配置下的 Blob / 自定义原生 Feature 保持可用。此有限组合仍待共享目标与 codec 方案复查。严格 IndexedDB 不声明允许最终镜像后等待外部 WAL 的能力，该组合在业务 I/O 前拒绝。

localStorage/sessionStorage/Cookie 可用 `redo: true` 显式启用文本事务与多键写，并同时选择 `journal.redoWal: logger.wal`。该组合要求真实 Web Locks；所有参与者借用同一个真实、可见最新 pending 的原 WAL 对象。仅目标同名或不同 memoryLogStore 不构成共享。浏览器同源 popup 可直接借用 opener 持有的精确 Logger/WAL；持久恢复可用另一个 IDB 后端的 storageLogStore 作为单拥有者载体，不能用待增强文本后端给自己承载 WAL。

原 transaction owner 管理 text-only scope，读取自身 draft；先完整编码，再 wal.begin，顺序应用、binlog、complete，之后发布一次失效提示和成功。应用或 complete 失败会停止该实例准入并保留 pending，重开或已打开的参与 peer 在物理保护内先恢复再读取。回调失败不应用 draft。未选 redo 时原标量与同步行为保持；选中异步 journal 后同步入口沿原 ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY 拒绝。redo 不宣称原生原子提交；undo/atomicBinlog/atomicUndo 与 raw 原生 Feature 句柄在该组合中修改前拒绝。独立 WAL 缓存之间的自动跨页恢复不作保证。
同一实例的 draft 活跃时，该实例根入口的读取、写入与另一事务立即报 `WRITE_CONFLICT`；独立调用方显式指定 `ConcurrencyPolicy.wait()` 也不会排队。回调内使用已提供的 scope。该隔离避免回调重入等待自身持有的 Web Lock；同实例排队 wait 尚未兑现。其它实例仍沿原 Web Locks 等待或取消，未选 redo 的原有行为保持。

Cookie 的 `redo: true` 复用同一原事务/WAL 协议；普通和 redo 写入共用原 cookie 编码、4096-byte 校验、固定 scope 与可见性检查。批量读取仍由同一原解析器读取一次可见 header，再合入当前 draft。redo 模式把 maxAge 在准备时转换为绝对 expiresAt 镜像，重放不续期；超过原生 Date 域的 maxAge 只在该新组合修改前拒绝，普通 Cookie maxAge 域和 Max-Age 优先级不变。该模式仅记录 JS 可见 cookie，HttpOnly/未知 scope 的原限制保持。
Browser backends for `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, cookies, and IndexedDB. Install the selected backend into `@migaia/storage-host`; the host owns preparation and cleanup.

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/storage-web @migaia/storage-host @migaia/storage-contract

blocks.text: Examples require an ESM browser environment with top-level `await`. Select a backend whose native browser API is available.
Prints `dark`. Disposing the host releases owned listeners and connections; it does not clear persistent browser data.

rows: text, bytes, records, native transactions, indexes

blocks.text: Each entry also exports its opaque backend kind and precise options/store types. The `plugins/*` entries export the same plugin functions. Pass native options first and an optional Feature record second. Import shared capabilities and context types directly from `@migaia/storage-contract`.
Memory, `createStorageHost`, `defineFeature`, and backend authoring belong to `@migaia/storage-host`. Entity repositories, schema adapters, and storage codecs belong to `@migaia/storage-host/entity`.

Unique entity writes require a real record transaction or the backend’s native atomic value-commit endpoint. Built-in browser backends provide it. A custom value-only backend without `core.registerValueCommit` rejects unique writes with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before schema work or mutation; ordinary KV remains available. See the host entity guide for the authoring contract.

`store.use(kv)` provides `getMany`, `setMany`, `removeMany`, and `removeByPrefix`. IndexedDB executes a batch in one native transaction and supports string, number, Date, binary, and tuple keys. String keys retain the same data as the original single-key methods. Reads preserve input order and duplicate positions, missing values are `undefined`, and deletion returns the actual count. Canonical duplicate write keys reject with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before I/O. Empty batches enter neither the pipeline nor a native transaction.

localStorage, sessionStorage, and Cookie support batch reads. Multi-key writes require WAL and reject with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before mutation when it is absent. The default namespace codec retains the string `sw1` layout and uses a separate `sw2` layout for typed keys. `keys()` still lists strings; namespace cleanup covers both layouts. A custom codec must provide both `encodeStorageKey` and `decodeStorageKey` to read non-string batch keys; otherwise those keys reject before native I/O.

All three channels share one native readwrite transaction. Only methods on the supplied scope participate. Completion waits for the actual native terminal; failures roll back that transaction. Do not await timers, network calls, or an independent root write inside the callback. An inactive native transaction fails with `TRANSACTION_FAILED`, retaining the native cause; callbacks are never resumed from a guard request.
The optional `features/reactive` entry adds `.live()` to supported query chains. It owns one service per installed Feature and attaches its source on first use. The caller owns the reactive Runtime.

Browser sources retain eventual visibility: local storage is document-eventual, session storage top-level-context-eventual, cookies origin-js-visible-eventual, and IndexedDB origin-eventual. Their original 1000 ms reconciliation remains. These are invalidation hints, not replication or a guarantee that arbitrary raw writers are observed immediately.

items: Text methods accept string keys and string values. `get` returns `null` for missing text; records return `undefined`.
`clearValues` affects only the text channel. `clearAll` affects the channels and namespace owned by that backend.
Same-key cross-channel writes fail with `DUPLICATE_KEY`; explicit `conflictPolicy: 'replace'` replaces displaced channels atomically.
Cookie scope is fixed at installation. HttpOnly cookies remain invisible; `has: false` does not prove their absence.
Disposal seals new work and drains admitted work. Explicit cleanup reports failure through its returned Promise; errors preserve their original cause chain.
After host installation starts, failure rejects with `@migaia/storage-host` `BACKEND_INSTALL_FAILED`; the original browser error remains in its cause chain.
Branch on `(source, code)`. Web errors use `@migaia/storage-web`; shared concurrency, cancellation, and owner errors retain their module identity.

blocks.text: See the usage guide for options, native activity, and lifecycle details.

IndexedDB exposes native text invalidation through `store.watch(key, ctx?)`. Its `capabilities.changeFeed` is `true` only after the instance admits this realm's IndexedDB and BroadcastChannel; an unadmitted watch throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Hints carry the original host organization UUID and tell the consumer to reread committed native data. They provide neither historical replay nor one event per write. Dispose the iterator after use through its original `dispose()` method.

IndexedDB natively provides `ttl`: `store.use(ttl)` exposes `expire`, `remaining` and `persist` for text, bytes and record targets; transactions use `scope.use(ttl)`. A `setMany` entry's `ttlMs` commits or rolls back with its value in the same native transaction. Entries have no deadline by default. Expired point reads, enumeration and index queries return absence and lazily remove data through the original transaction, revision and change paths; no cleanup timer runs. Deadlines advance through the installed scheduler from one local epoch anchor captured at installation. Default-clock deadlines remain comparable across pages and reopening. IndexedDB has no vector channel, so vector TTL targets fail before I/O with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.

Text organization views use the configured namespace for the host default and namespace + "/" + orgId for every other organization. The same captured native client, namespace codec and Cookie scope remain in use. A configured namespace ending in "/" plus a canonical UUID rejects before native I/O; a bare UUID remains valid. dropOrg clears only that target, preserves other organizations and plugin prefixes, and leaves existing views reusable. Borrowed entities retain the original native atomic unique writer. IndexedDB maps dbName by the same rule. dropOrg makes the target connection close-pending, drains native transactions, and waits for that target's deleteDatabase request. New opens wait for the same request; existing views reopen afterward. Other instances close through their original versionchange handler. A foreign connection that refuses to close keeps native deletion pending; the host never resumes opening early and lets a late deletion destroy new data.

localStorage declares changeFeed:true only after registering the actual localStorage and storage event source of the same Window. A Storage-like injection alone remains false. Original watch/subscribeChanges combine committed writes from this instance with native cross-document events, filtered by storageArea, namespace codec, and organization; host disposal releases the listener. The receiving controller numbers hints locally, without a native writer history sequence. Reread current data: delivery is neither per-write nor a native notification for other instances in the same page. Organization views retain watch with runtime capability admission and no backend close authority.

Select `indexedDbBlobFeature` from the dedicated subpath. It adds `store.api.blobs` and `scope.api.blobs`. Blob/File values use native structured clone; File name, type and lastModified survive reopening. The default store is `__migaia_blobs__`. Declare a different name with `{ storeName }`; declaration collisions fail before opening. Blob requests share the original record transaction, cancellation, quota normalization and rollback. Organization views use their actual database and original transaction owner. The Feature grants no database disposal method.

IndexedDB supports `storageLogStore(hostOrOrg, 'indexed-db', { prefix })` from `@migaia/storage-host/journal`. Its private rows use an array-key namespace in the existing META store. Business `clearAll` leaves history intact; organization deletion invalidates old log handles, while the original business view can reopen. In cached mode, dispose a log before opening the same physical organization and prefix again. Native transactions commit head/state/records together and publish the cached index from the actual complete event.

Native Web Locks retain the original lifetime exclusion and cached path; a conflicting open reports LOCK_REJECTED. Without Web Locks or an actual private-factory declaration, the original namespace declares `indexExclusive:false`. storageLogStore remains available: each operation recovers/reads current lastSeq, state and records inside the original journal-store readwrite transaction, retaining no index across operations. Injected factories use the original cached path when Web Locks are available. `journalFactoryIsPrivate:true` applies only to an actual data universe confined to this realm without forwarding shared persistent storage; that path retains the original logical lock and cached owner. Object identity alone never proves isolation. This namespace support does not enable automatic global capture or opt-in undo by itself.

sections.heading: IndexedDB global journal and explicit undo

blocks.text: Inside the Host `journal` initializer, open native binlog and undo stores with the current org's `storageLogStore`, then pass those same objects to the logger plugins and `atomicBinlog` / `atomicUndo`. A logger with the undo plugin requires explicit `indexedDbUndo: true`; omission or false reports `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before the business native transaction. The configured backend and org views expose `undo(txId)`, restored through the original transaction builder.

Text, bytes, records, clear and absolute TTL metadata retain their actual write order in one native transaction, including repeated writes. Only native complete publishes the log index; rollback does not advance its sequence. A first org read also prepares that org's once-only configuration, and lazy expiry deletion commits with its log. All contract writers maintain native point revisions and retain tombstones after delete or clear, so clear/recreate by another non-journal contract handle also rejects stale undo with `UNDO_CONFLICT` before restoring any target. Undo compares physical images and restores the original absolute deadline without extending expiry.

Native Features borrow IDBDatabase / IDBTransaction directly, beyond the current text, bytes and record image domain. An active commit journal rejects this combination with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before handing out the native handle. Blob and custom native Features remain available without a journal and with telemetry-only configuration. This limited combination awaits review of shared targets and codecs. Strict IndexedDB does not declare support for external WAL I/O after final image capture; that combination rejects before business I/O.

localStorage/sessionStorage/Cookie explicitly enable text transactions and multi-key writes with `redo: true` plus `journal.redoWal: logger.wal`. Native Web Locks are required. Every participant borrows the same actual WAL object with current pending visibility; matching targets or separate memoryLogStore caches do not establish sharing. A same-origin popup can directly borrow its opener's exact Logger/WAL. For persistence, one owner may hold an original storageLogStore on a separate IndexedDB backend; the enhanced text backend cannot carry its own WAL.

The original transaction owner manages the text-only scope and read-own-draft behavior. It finishes encoding before wal.begin, then applies ordered assignments, binlog and complete, and finally publishes one invalidation and success. Apply/completion failure seals that instance and preserves pending; reopening or an already-open participating peer recovers under native protection before reading. Callback rollback applies nothing. Ordinary scalar/sync behavior remains when redo is absent; selected asynchronous journaling retains the original ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY guard. Redo does not claim native atomicity. Undo/atomicBinlog/atomicUndo and raw native Feature handles reject before mutation in this combination. Automatic cross-page recovery between independent WAL caches is not promised.

While one instance has an active draft, its root reads, writes and other transactions immediately reject with `WRITE_CONFLICT`, including independent callers selecting `ConcurrencyPolicy.wait()`. Use the supplied scope inside the callback. This isolation prevents callback reentry from waiting on its own Web Lock; same-instance queued wait is not provided. Other instances still wait or cancel through native Web Locks. Behavior without redo remains unchanged.

Cookie `redo: true` reuses this same transaction/WAL protocol. Ordinary and redo writes share the original cookie encoding, 4096-byte limit, fixed scope and visibility checks. Batch reads still parse one native visible header and merge the current draft. Redo resolves maxAge to an absolute expiresAt image during preparation, so replay never renews it. Values outside the native Date domain reject before mutation only in this new combination; ordinary Cookie maxAge and Max-Age precedence remain unchanged. Only JS-visible cookies participate; original HttpOnly/unknown-scope limits remain.

Ordinary localStorage, sessionStorage and Cookie stores declare `capabilities.batch: false`; IndexedDB and explicit redo/WAL stores declare it true. Native IndexedDB handles are unavailable with commit journaling and reject with source `@migaia/storage-contract`, code `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. IndexedDB does not provide a vector engine. The repository website stays on published storage-web 0.0.8 until the new host module are published.

Import entity codecs from `@migaia/storage-host/entity`. `jsonCodec` has `output: text` and uses strict portable JSON. `structuredCodec` has `output: structured` and delegates storage to a record backend. `binaryCodec` has `output: binary` and accepts `Uint8Array`. `selectCodec` selects a direct channel, a supported fallback, or rejection from the backend's actual capabilities.

Portable JSON rejects unsupported objects and cycles. For `Map` and `Set`, adapt `defineCollectionsJsonCodec` from `@migaia/serialize/codecs/collections-json` with `fromValueCodec` from `@migaia/storage-host/authoring/codec`. A structured backend can instead save supported built-ins and cycles with `structuredCodec`.

`structuredCodec.encode/decode` returns the original value; the record backend performs copying. IndexedDB uses native structured cloning. The memory backend copies byte views and uses `structuredClone` for records. `binaryCodec` validates and retains the original byte view, while the backend owns its write snapshot. These codecs neither rebuild application class instances nor validate the domain schema.

The schema handles domain representation; the codec handles the saved format. Reads call `codec.decode`, migrate the saved representation, call `schema.decode`, and validate the domain value. A text-only backend rejects structured output with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` rather than silently converting it to JSON.
Use the selected browser plugin with the real host. The examples require native browser APIs; an injected port does not turn a Node process into a browser.

Installation completes preparation before publishing stores. Reuse a plugin definition to create separate owned installations; do not share a store already owned by another host. Use explicit IDs when installing the same kind more than once. Repeated disposal shares its completion Promise, and closed stores cannot be reopened.

A supplied Storage port must implement `length`, `getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`, `key`, and `clear`. Installation probes availability while preserving existing data. Refused host access yields `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`; invalid configuration yields `INVALID_CONFIG`. Native quota failure yields `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. The advertised 5 MiB limit is an estimate, not a browser quota guarantee.

The default namespace codec uses a UTF-8 length prefix, for example `sw1:3:app:theme`. Its decoder skips malformed or foreign entries. A custom codec owns collision avoidance and format migration. `clearValues` snapshots matching physical keys before deleting them; a native failure can leave a partial clear and retains the failing key.

`namespace` defaults to `default`; `document` defaults to `globalThis.document`. Scope defaults to `{ path: '/' }` and remains fixed for all writes and deletes. A supplied domain must be nonempty and contain no whitespace or semicolons. `sameSite: 'none'` and `partitioned: true` require `secure: true`.

Write options accept a valid `expires: Date` or integer `maxAge`. Expired writes delete the cookie. The 4096-byte bound covers the complete assignment, including attributes. A same-name cookie visible in several scopes yields `COOKIE_SCOPE_AMBIGUOUS`; a normal write that is not visible afterwards yields `WRITE_FAILED`. JS cannot observe HttpOnly entries or guarantee server-side deletion.

Use `store.use(kv)` for `getMany(keys)`, `setMany(entries)`, `removeMany(keys)`, and `removeByPrefix(prefix)`. Each nonempty IndexedDB batch enters one pipeline and one native transaction; a later channel conflict rolls back the complete batch. Reads retain duplicate positions and `undefined` missing values. Removal counts a canonical key once. Duplicate canonical write keys reject before any I/O, and `ttlMs` requires the TTL capability. Empty batches return without pipeline, hooks, or native requests.

Text Web backends use synchronous native reads for `getMany`; Cookie reads one visible header snapshot. Without WAL, multi-key writes and prefix deletion reject with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before mutation. A loop over public `set` calls is not an atomic batch.

The default namespace codec retains the original string `sw1` layout and gives non-string batch keys a separate top-level `sw2` layout using the shared canonical key codec. Every old string key remains distinct from a typed key. `keys()` retains `string[]`; namespace clear removes both layouts. A custom `INamespaceCodec` can add `encodeStorageKey(namespace,key)` and `decodeStorageKey(namespace,physicalKey)`. Provide both and keep all key types collision-free. Without this pair, new non-string batch reads reject before native I/O while original string data and calls remain unchanged.

`dbName` defaults to `storage-web`; `kvStoreName`, `bytesStoreName`, and `recordsStoreName` default to `kv`, `bytes`, and `records`. Names must be nonempty, distinct, and avoid reserved internal stores. `factory` and `keyRange` default to `globalThis.indexedDB` and `globalThis.IDBKeyRange`. Optional `owner.label` is diagnostic metadata, never a lock identity.

The host opens and prepares the selected database before publication. Missing internal stores are created by a native version upgrade. `onversionchange` closes the old connection. A blocked open rejects instead of publishing an unprepared backend. `cleanupLegacyRecords` defaults to `false`; enabling it removes the legacy store only after successful migration.

A transaction scope covers text, bytes, records, and index maintenance in one original native transaction. `scope.use(kv)` adds structured-key batch methods; `scope.use(records)` exposes queries and bounded prefix removal. Root text keys remain strings. Record and scoped text keys follow `IStorageKey` from `@migaia/storage-contract`, including number, Date, ArrayBuffer, and nested arrays.

Await only native operations and activity-preserving microtasks within the callback. A timer or network wait can end the native activity window. A later method then fails `TRANSACTION_FAILED` with the native cause; catching that method failure does not turn the transaction into a commit. Scope methods lose admission when the callback closes. Finalizers use separate authentic views of the same transaction. Accepted operations, iterators, callbacks, and finalizers drain before resource release.

`setBytes` snapshots input bytes. Record writes use structured cloning and reject unsupported values with `SERIALIZE_FAILED`. Native completion precedes notification. A listener failure is reported and cannot undo a committed write.
Import the neutral repository owner from `@migaia/storage-host/entity` and connect it to the actual installed IndexedDB store.

The host entity module owns schemas, versioned envelopes, migration, and projection. Ordinary reads materialize the declared version without writing it back; explicit `migrate()` performs persistence. Native secondary-index readiness is checked on the actual current transaction snapshot. Unique writes require a real record transaction or the native atomic value-commit endpoint registered by the backend during installation with `core.registerValueCommit`. Built-in browser backends provide the required path. Custom value-only backends without that endpoint reject unique `put` and `migrate` with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before schema work or mutation; ordinary KV access remains available. A `sync` projection alone does not provide cross-page atomicity.
Install `@migaia/reactive` explicitly when using the following example. Pass Features as the backend plugin’s second argument.

`ready` observes initial work, `refresh()` joins active work or requests a new generation, and `state` is a readonly computed. `keepPreviousData` defaults to `true`; `equals` defaults to no suppression. Optional `scope` and `matches` filter invalidations; predicate failures report and refresh conservatively. `timeoutMs` applies per generation, while `signal` cancels the query lifetime. Cleanup leaves the caller-owned Runtime usable.

Sources are eventual and preserve native visibility. Local/session/cookie/IndexedDB use hybrid invalidation with 1000 ms reconciliation; memory from `@migaia/storage-host` uses instance-local push without polling. No source promises immediate capture of arbitrary external writes.

Inspect both `source` and `code`. After host installation starts, failure rejects with the host's `BACKEND_INSTALL_FAILED`; its cause chain retains the original browser error. Native Web failures retain cause and stack under coded `StorageError`; shared cancellation, locks, owner validation, schema, and codec failures keep their original module identity. `ABORTED` retains the original cancellation reason. Retry concurrency according to `ConcurrencyPolicy` from the contract, rather than retrying committed notifications.

`host.dispose()` seals admission, cancels queued members, drains admitted work, then releases listeners and connections. Direct explicit backend cleanup propagates `BACKEND_DISPOSE_FAILED` with original errors reachable. Repeated explicit calls share their Promise. The async-disposal symbol has its own report-only completion projection over the same cleanup. A failure never makes a closed backend reusable.

Replace direct factories with the four backend plugins installed through `@migaia/storage-host`. Import memory and host primitives from that module, entities, schemas, and storage codecs from its `entity` entry. Replace old reactive wrappers and host live-query calls with an explicit `reactiveFeature(targetKind)` and `query.live()`. No legacy factory aliases are exported.

IndexedDB exposes native text invalidation through `store.watch(key, ctx?)`. Its `capabilities.changeFeed` is `true` only after the instance admits this realm's IndexedDB and BroadcastChannel; an unadmitted watch throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Hints carry the original host organization UUID and tell the consumer to reread committed native data. They provide neither historical replay nor one event per write. Dispose the iterator after use through its original `dispose()` method.

IndexedDB natively provides `ttl`: `store.use(ttl)` exposes `expire`, `remaining` and `persist` for text, bytes and record targets; transactions use `scope.use(ttl)`. A `setMany` entry's `ttlMs` commits or rolls back with its value in the same native transaction. Entries have no deadline by default. Expired point reads, enumeration and index queries return absence and lazily remove data through the original transaction, revision and change paths; no cleanup timer runs. Deadlines advance through the installed scheduler from one local epoch anchor captured at installation. Default-clock deadlines remain comparable across pages and reopening. IndexedDB has no vector channel, so vector TTL targets fail before I/O with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.

Text organization views use the configured namespace for the host default and namespace + "/" + orgId for every other organization. The same captured native client, namespace codec and Cookie scope remain in use. A configured namespace ending in "/" plus a canonical UUID rejects before native I/O; a bare UUID remains valid. dropOrg clears only that target, preserves other organizations and plugin prefixes, and leaves existing views reusable. Borrowed entities retain the original native atomic unique writer. IndexedDB maps dbName by the same rule. dropOrg makes the target connection close-pending, drains native transactions, and waits for that target's deleteDatabase request. New opens wait for the same request; existing views reopen afterward. Other instances close through their original versionchange handler. A foreign connection that refuses to close keeps native deletion pending; the host never resumes opening early and lets a late deletion destroy new data.

localStorage declares changeFeed:true only after registering the actual localStorage and storage event source of the same Window. A Storage-like injection alone remains false. Original watch/subscribeChanges combine committed writes from this instance with native cross-document events, filtered by storageArea, namespace codec, and organization; host disposal releases the listener. The receiving controller numbers hints locally, without a native writer history sequence. Reread current data: delivery is neither per-write nor a native notification for other instances in the same page. Organization views retain watch with runtime capability admission and no backend close authority.

Select `indexedDbBlobFeature` from the dedicated subpath. It adds `store.api.blobs` and `scope.api.blobs`. Blob/File values use native structured clone; File name, type and lastModified survive reopening. The default store is `__migaia_blobs__`. Declare a different name with `{ storeName }`; declaration collisions fail before opening. Blob requests share the original record transaction, cancellation, quota normalization and rollback. Organization views use their actual database and original transaction owner. The Feature grants no database disposal method.

IndexedDB supports `storageLogStore(hostOrOrg, 'indexed-db', { prefix })` from `@migaia/storage-host/journal`. Its private rows use an array-key namespace in the existing META store. Business `clearAll` leaves history intact; organization deletion invalidates old log handles, while the original business view can reopen. In cached mode, dispose a log before opening the same physical organization and prefix again. Native transactions commit head/state/records together and publish the cached index from the actual complete event.

Native Web Locks retain the original lifetime exclusion and cached path; a conflicting open reports LOCK_REJECTED. Without Web Locks or an actual private-factory declaration, the original namespace declares `indexExclusive:false`. storageLogStore remains available: each operation recovers/reads current lastSeq, state and records inside the original journal-store readwrite transaction, retaining no index across operations. Injected factories use the original cached path when Web Locks are available. `journalFactoryIsPrivate:true` applies only to an actual data universe confined to this realm without forwarding shared persistent storage; that path retains the original logical lock and cached owner. Object identity alone never proves isolation. This namespace support does not enable automatic global capture or opt-in undo by itself.

sections.heading: IndexedDB global journal and explicit undo

blocks.text: Inside the Host `journal` initializer, open native binlog and undo stores with the current org's `storageLogStore`, then pass those same objects to the logger plugins and `atomicBinlog` / `atomicUndo`. A logger with the undo plugin requires explicit `indexedDbUndo: true`; omission or false reports `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before the business native transaction. The configured backend and org views expose `undo(txId)`, restored through the original transaction builder.

Text, bytes, records, clear and absolute TTL metadata retain their actual write order in one native transaction, including repeated writes. Only native complete publishes the log index; rollback does not advance its sequence. A first org read also prepares that org's once-only configuration, and lazy expiry deletion commits with its log. All contract writers maintain native point revisions and retain tombstones after delete or clear, so clear/recreate by another non-journal contract handle also rejects stale undo with `UNDO_CONFLICT` before restoring any target. Undo compares physical images and restores the original absolute deadline without extending expiry.

Native Features borrow IDBDatabase / IDBTransaction directly, beyond the current text, bytes and record image domain. An active commit journal rejects this combination with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before handing out the native handle. Blob and custom native Features remain available without a journal and with telemetry-only configuration. This limited combination awaits review of shared targets and codecs. Strict IndexedDB does not declare support for external WAL I/O after final image capture; that combination rejects before business I/O.

localStorage/sessionStorage/Cookie explicitly enable text transactions and multi-key writes with `redo: true` plus `journal.redoWal: logger.wal`. Native Web Locks are required. Every participant borrows the same actual WAL object with current pending visibility; matching targets or separate memoryLogStore caches do not establish sharing. A same-origin popup can directly borrow its opener's exact Logger/WAL. For persistence, one owner may hold an original storageLogStore on a separate IndexedDB backend; the enhanced text backend cannot carry its own WAL.

The original transaction owner manages the text-only scope and read-own-draft behavior. It finishes encoding before wal.begin, then applies ordered assignments, binlog and complete, and finally publishes one invalidation and success. Apply/completion failure seals that instance and preserves pending; reopening or an already-open participating peer recovers under native protection before reading. Callback rollback applies nothing. Ordinary scalar/sync behavior remains when redo is absent; selected asynchronous journaling retains the original ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY guard. Redo does not claim native atomicity. Undo/atomicBinlog/atomicUndo and raw native Feature handles reject before mutation in this combination. Automatic cross-page recovery between independent WAL caches is not promised.

While one instance has an active draft, its root reads, writes and other transactions immediately reject with `WRITE_CONFLICT`, including independent callers selecting `ConcurrencyPolicy.wait()`. Use the supplied scope inside the callback. This isolation prevents callback reentry from waiting on its own Web Lock; same-instance queued wait is not provided. Other instances still wait or cancel through native Web Locks. Behavior without redo remains unchanged.

Cookie `redo: true` reuses this same transaction/WAL protocol. Ordinary and redo writes share the original cookie encoding, 4096-byte limit, fixed scope and visibility checks. Batch reads still parse one native visible header and merge the current draft. Redo resolves maxAge to an absolute expiresAt image during preparation, so replay never renews it. Values outside the native Date domain reject before mutation only in this new combination; ordinary Cookie maxAge and Max-Age precedence remain unchanged. Only JS-visible cookies participate; original HttpOnly/unknown-scope limits remain.

`host.dispose()` 封闭新准入、取消排队成员、排空已接纳工作，再释放监听器与连接。显式后端清理以 `BACKEND_DISPOSE_FAILED` 传播失败，原始错误可达。重复显式调用共享 Promise，异步释放符号通过同一次清理提供独立的只报告完成投影。失败不会让已关闭后端复活。

symbols.purpose: Table of this package’s stable error codes; values are the strings on error.code. `INDEX_BACKFILL_FAILED` identifies backfill and failed-readiness persistence failing together on a native AggregateError.
symbols.core:
unavailable: `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: storage is disabled or missing (private mode); pick `memoryBackendPlugin` from `@migaia/storage-host` or ask for access.
quotaExceeded: `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`: the browser quota is full; delete data or use IndexedDB.
valueTooLarge: `VALUE_TOO_LARGE`: a cookie value is over 4 KB.
serializeFailed: `SERIALIZE_FAILED`: encoding the value failed.
deserializeFailed: `DESERIALIZE_FAILED`: decoding the stored value failed.
transactionFailed: `TRANSACTION_FAILED`: the IndexedDB transaction failed or the callback threw.
duplicateKey: `DUPLICATE_KEY`: the key is used by another channel; pass `conflictPolicy: "replace"` to overwrite.
versionUnsupported: `VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`: stored data is newer than this code.
extensionFailed: `EXTENSION_FAILED`: a schema, codec or comparator threw.
writeFailed: `WRITE_FAILED`: a written cookie was not visible afterwards.
cookieScopeAmbiguous: `COOKIE_SCOPE_AMBIGUOUS`: one cookie name is visible in several scopes.
invalidConfig: `INVALID_CONFIG`: an option or scope is invalid.
indexOrphan: `INDEX_ORPHAN`: an index points to a missing record; rebuild it.
indexUniqueConflict: `INDEX_UNIQUE_CONFLICT`: a unique index key belongs to another record.
indexQueryInvalidated: `INDEX_QUERY_INVALIDATED`: data changed during paging; restart the query.
liveQueryDisposed: `LIVE_QUERY_DISPOSED`: the live query was disposed; create a new one.
indexBackfillStale: `INDEX_BACKFILL_STALE`: an index backfill checkpoint expired; reconnect and retry.
indexBackfillFailed: `INDEX_BACKFILL_FAILED`: backfill and persisting failed readiness both failed. The native AggregateError keeps the primary error first in errors and as cause, followed by the persistence failure; inspect both original objects before retrying.
liveQueryDisposeFailed: `LIVE_QUERY_DISPOSE_FAILED`: query cleanup failed; see `errors`.
reactiveFeatureInvalid: `REACTIVE_FEATURE_INVALID`: the reactive Feature does not match the backend.
reactiveAdapterNotInstalled: `REACTIVE_ADAPTER_NOT_INSTALLED`: the backend id is not reactive.
reactiveAdapterFailed: `REACTIVE_ADAPTER_FAILED`: the adapter failed; later changes may recover.
reactiveAdapterDisposeFailed: `REACTIVE_ADAPTER_DISPOSE_FAILED`: adapter cleanup failed.
backendDisposeFailed: `BACKEND_DISPOSE_FAILED`: backend cleanup failed.

members.name: unavailable
members.description: A storage backend is unavailable because a private-mode probe fails or localStorage, IndexedDB, * or `document` is disabled or missing. * * The caller selects another installed backend or asks the user to enable storage access, rather * than retrying the same unavailable backend. Enforces the availability probe contract.

members.name: quotaExceeded
members.description: A write reaches the browser quota, such as `QuotaExceededError` or Firefox's * `NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED`. * * The caller removes unneeded data or selects IndexedDB. The failure persists until storage * conditions change.

members.name: valueTooLarge
members.description: A serialized cookie assignment exceeds the 4 KB limit. * * The caller shortens the value, name, or attributes, or stores the data in IndexedDB. The * library does not silently truncate the assignment.

members.name: serializeFailed
members.description: A native IndexedDB record or byte write fails while snapshotting its payload with * `structuredClone`, before asynchronous admission or physical mutation. * * The caller checks whether the value can be serialized. This is a data shape failure rather than * a backend failure.

members.name: deserializeFailed
members.description: A decoded IndexedDB cross-instance notification contains an invalid encoded key hint. * * The caller checks whether an external writer or newer version changes the stored data.

members.name: transactionFailed
members.description: A transaction or exclusive entity commit fails, including IndexedDB creation/commit, host * coordination, or a callback error outside the storage error family. * * The caller checks whether the transaction crosses the automatic commit boundary or its scope * escapes. Transient concurrency failures can be retried.

members.name: duplicateKey
members.description: A logical key conflicts across the value, bytes, and record channels without `conflictPolicy: * 'replace'`. * * The caller changes the key or explicitly selects `replace` to atomically remove the same key * from other channels.

members.name: versionUnsupported
members.description: The native IndexedDB schema version exceeds the version known to the current adapter. * * The caller upgrades the code or downgrades the data. Older code must not misread or overwrite * data from a newer version.

members.name: extensionFailed
members.description: An extension such as schema, codec, `namespaceCodec`, comparator, or diagnostic throws an * unclassified exception. * * The caller checks the extension implementation. `extensionStage` identifies the failed * extension, and `cause` retains the original exception.

members.name: writeFailed
members.description: A cookie is not visible after a write because the browser silently rejects it. * * The caller checks cookie attributes (`path`, `domain`, `SameSite`, and `secure`) and capacity. * Privacy policies may still remove the cookie asynchronously.

members.name: cookieScopeAmbiguous
members.description: Multiple visible cookie scopes share a name, so the target value's scope is ambiguous. * * The caller gives each scope a unique cookie name or fixes the scope at construction to avoid * ambiguity.

members.name: invalidConfig
members.description: Web adapter input or configuration validation fails. Covers cookie `SameSite`, `Secure`, * `Partitioned`, and scope settings; IndexedDB factory, store names, and `IDBKeyRange`; namespace * codecs; and browser backend options. * * Contract shape validation uses `storage-contract`'s `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. This code covers * adapter configuration only, as a local exception to unified argument validation. * * The caller corrects the configuration before retrying. The argument or configuration failure * persists until it changes.

members.name: indexOrphan
members.description: IndexedDB sidecar contains an index row whose authoritative record is absent. Callers should * repair or rebuild the index rather than treating the skipped row as a successful query result.

members.name: indexUniqueConflict
members.description: An indexed mutation would assign one logical unique key to two authoritative records. * Uniqueness is enforced inside the record/sidecar transaction; callers must choose a different * indexed value or remove the competing record before retrying.

members.name: indexQueryInvalidated
members.description: A native `iterateRecordIndex` page observed the global or scope mutation epoch change between * pages. Each page validates a short readonly transaction, then closes it before yielding; * callers must restart the query rather than trust a mixed snapshot.

members.name: liveQueryDisposed
members.description: A live-query consumer attempted to refresh after terminal disposal. Disposal cannot revive * subscriptions or owned reactive state; callers must create a new live query instead of reusing * the disposed handle.

members.name: indexBackfillStale
members.description: A backfill operation presented an expired owner, stale generation, or conflicting checkpoint. * The batch must be rejected and rolled back; callers should retry through a fresh repository * operation after the current handle is reacquired.

members.name: indexBackfillFailed
members.description: Secondary-index backfill failed and persisting its failed readiness also failed. The caller * inspects the native aggregate's original cause/errors before retrying; neither the primary * failure nor the persistence failure may be discarded.

members.name: liveQueryDisposeFailed
members.description: Live-query request or owned reactive cleanup collected one or more failures. Callers must treat * the query as terminal and inspect AggregateError.errors.

members.name: reactiveFeatureInvalid
members.description: A reactive feature descriptor, brand, provider seam, or adapter result is invalid. Callers must * correct the exact feature/backend pairing before retrying.

members.name: reactiveAdapterNotInstalled
members.description: The requested backend lacks its reactive adapter or is not installed. Callers must use an * installed adapter-bound backend ID, with no default fallback.

members.name: reactiveAdapterFailed
members.description: A reactive adapter event, poll, or authoritative read failed. Callers should observe the query * error state and allow a later invalidation or poll to recover.

members.name: reactiveAdapterDisposeFailed
members.description: Reactive adapter, poller, query, or service cleanup collected failures. Callers must treat the * adapter as terminal and inspect AggregateError.errors.

members.name: backendDisposeFailed
members.description: Direct backend quiescence, transport, connection, or channel cleanup collected failures. * Callers must treat the backend as terminal and inspect all errors.

sections.content: Import StorageErrorCode from @migaia/storage-web, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use StorageErrorCode when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when StorageErrorCode does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
unavailable: `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`: storage is disabled or missing (private mode); pick `memoryBackendPlugin` from `@migaia/storage-host` or ask for access.
quotaExceeded: `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`: the browser quota is full; delete data or use IndexedDB.
valueTooLarge: `VALUE_TOO_LARGE`: a cookie value is over 4 KB.
serializeFailed: `SERIALIZE_FAILED`: encoding the value failed.
deserializeFailed: `DESERIALIZE_FAILED`: decoding the stored value failed.
transactionFailed: `TRANSACTION_FAILED`: the IndexedDB transaction failed or the callback threw.
duplicateKey: `DUPLICATE_KEY`: the key is used by another channel; pass `conflictPolicy: "replace"` to overwrite.
versionUnsupported: `VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`: stored data is newer than this code.
extensionFailed: `EXTENSION_FAILED`: a schema, codec or comparator threw.
writeFailed: `WRITE_FAILED`: a written cookie was not visible afterwards.
cookieScopeAmbiguous: `COOKIE_SCOPE_AMBIGUOUS`: one cookie name is visible in several scopes.
invalidConfig: `INVALID_CONFIG`: an option or scope is invalid.
indexOrphan: `INDEX_ORPHAN`: an index points to a missing record; rebuild it.
indexUniqueConflict: `INDEX_UNIQUE_CONFLICT`: a unique index key belongs to another record.
indexQueryInvalidated: `INDEX_QUERY_INVALIDATED`: data changed during paging; restart the query.
liveQueryDisposed: `LIVE_QUERY_DISPOSED`: the live query was disposed; create a new one.
indexBackfillStale: `INDEX_BACKFILL_STALE`: an index backfill checkpoint expired; reconnect and retry.
indexBackfillFailed: `INDEX_BACKFILL_FAILED`: backfill and persisting failed readiness both failed. The native AggregateError keeps the primary error first in errors and as cause, followed by the persistence failure; inspect both original objects before retrying.
liveQueryDisposeFailed: `LIVE_QUERY_DISPOSE_FAILED`: query cleanup failed; see `errors`.
reactiveFeatureInvalid: `REACTIVE_FEATURE_INVALID`: the reactive Feature does not match the backend.
reactiveAdapterNotInstalled: `REACTIVE_ADAPTER_NOT_INSTALLED`: the backend id is not reactive.
reactiveAdapterFailed: `REACTIVE_ADAPTER_FAILED`: the adapter failed; later changes may recover.
reactiveAdapterDisposeFailed: `REACTIVE_ADAPTER_DISPOSE_FAILED`: adapter cleanup failed.
backendDisposeFailed: `BACKEND_DISPOSE_FAILED`: backend cleanup failed.

symbols.core:
cookieValueInvalid: Cookie text writes received a value that is not a string.
cookieMaxAgeInvalid: Cookie Max-Age is not a safe integer number of seconds.
cookieExpiresInvalid: Cookie Expires is not an authentic valid Date.
cookieRedoScopeMismatch: A visible cookie with the same name remains in an unknown scope during redo.
cookieRedoWriteInvisible: A cookie assignment was not visible through the active fixed scope.
indexedDbJournalFactoryIsolationInvalid: A private-factory declaration is neither true nor omitted.
indexedDbJournalFactoryMustBeInjected: The known shared realm factory cannot be declared a private data universe.
storageBatchKeysInvalid: Batch keys must be a finite caller-provided array.
storageBatchEntriesInvalid: Batch writes require an array of key and value entries.
storageBatchDuplicateKey: A batch repeats one canonical logical storage-key identity.
indexedDbOwnerInvalid: An owner label must be an object with an optional string label.
indexedDbSchemaDeclarationInvalid: A Feature attempted to declare an object store after the original opener sealed.
indexedDbTransactionEndedEarly: The native transaction ended before the backend chose its commit outcome.
storageValueInvalid: The native text channel received a value that is not a string.
storageBytesInvalid: The native binary channel received a value that is not a Uint8Array.
namespaceCodecEncodeInvalid: A namespace encoder returned a non-string physical key.
namespaceCodecDecodeInvalid: A namespace decoder returned neither a string key nor undefined for another namespace.
namespaceTypedCodecInvalid: Typed namespace support supplies only one direction or a non-callable method.
namespaceCodecInvalid: The original namespace codec lacks callable encode and decode methods.
namespaceKeyInvalid: String-key encoding received a non-string namespace or key.
namespacePhysicalKeyInvalid: Namespace decoding received a non-string namespace or physical key.
webStorageInjectionInvalid: Injected Web Storage lacks part of the required storage interface.
webStorageLengthInvalid: The live Web Storage length is not a nonnegative safe integer.
webStorageKeyInvalid: Live Web Storage enumeration did not provide a string key for a visible index.
webStorageKeyDuplicate: Live Web Storage enumeration returned the same physical key more than once.
indexedDbChangeHintKeyInvalid: An IndexedDB coordination hint contains an undecodable storage key.
indexedDbUpgradeTransactionMissing: An IndexedDB upgrade event omitted the platform-owned upgrade transaction.
cookieDocumentBecameInvalid: An admitted cookie document stopped exposing its cookie property as a string.
liveQueryDisposeFailed: Several live-query cleanup failures are summarized after disposal.
reactiveFeatureInvalid: A reactive provider, feature or adapter descriptor has an invalid shape.
reactiveAdapterNotInstalled: The requested backend has no installed reactive adapter.
reactiveAdapterFailed: An adapter event, polling operation or authoritative read failed recoverably.
reactiveAdapterDisposeFailed: Reactive adapter or service cleanup produced aggregated failures.
liveQueryFailed: A live-query extension callback failed and its original cause is retained.
backendDisposeFailed: Direct backend cleanup failed and is reported through the storage boundary.
indexOrphan: An index sidecar row has no authoritative entity record.
indexQueryInvalidated: Concurrent mutation invalidated a native paged index query.
liveQueryDisposed: A permanently disposed live query was used again and must be recreated.
indexBackfillStale: The index backfill handle is stale and the query must retry.
indexBackfillProjectionTooLarge: Backfill projection work exceeded its fixed bound before sidecar writes.
indexBackfillDecodedTooLarge: Decoded backfill payload exceeded its fixed bound before issuing a partial batch.

capabilities: Backend-supplied `IStorageCapabilities` describing callable channels and their limits; admission snapshots these facts once.
get: Reads a string value from the L0 channel of the supplied backend, using optional operation intent.

A promise of the stored string, or null when the key is absent; backend failures reject.
set: Writes one string value through the supplied backend’s commit path and selected existing-key policy.
set.key: String key selected by the application for this channel; the same spelling identifies a later read or removal.
set.value: Application-produced string payload; encode non-string data before using this channel.
set.ctx: Optional caller-authored `IWriteOptions`: `signal` has boolean `aborted` and callable `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`; `timeoutMs` is a nonnegative safe integer including 0; `pageSize` is an integer from 1 to 4096. `orgId` is an optional canonical lowercase UUID. remove: Removes the application-selected string entry from the supplied backend’s value channel.
remove.key: String key selected by the application for this channel; the same spelling identifies a later read or removal.
remove.ctx: Optional caller-authored `IOperationContext`: `signal` is an object with boolean `aborted` and callable `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`; `timeoutMs` is a nonnegative safe integer including 0; `pageSize` is an integer from 1 to 4096. `orgId` is an optional canonical lowercase UUID, including the zero UUID. A `Promise<void>` indicating removal has settled; backend failures reject.
has: Checks whether one string-channel key currently exists in the backend.
has.key: String key selected by the application for this channel; the same spelling identifies a later read or removal.

A promise of the existence flag for the selected key.
keys: Lists visible string-channel keys from the backend; visibility and opaque entries remain backend capabilities.
keys.ctx: Optional caller-authored `IOperationContext`: `signal` is an object with boolean `aborted` and callable `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`; `timeoutMs` is a nonnegative safe integer including 0; `pageSize` is an integer from 1 to 4096. `orgId` is an optional canonical lowercase UUID, including the zero UUID. Each field defaults to `undefined`. Concrete backends execute cancellation, timeouts and paging.
A promise of visible string keys; ordering is not fixed by this interface.
clearValues: Clears the backend’s string value channel while leaving distinct byte and record channels to their own clear operations.
clearValues.ctx: Optional caller-authored `IOperationContext`: `signal` is an object with boolean `aborted` and callable `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`; `timeoutMs` is a nonnegative safe integer including 0; `pageSize` is an integer from 1 to 4096. `orgId` is an optional canonical lowercase UUID, including the zero UUID. Each field defaults to `undefined`. Concrete backends execute cancellation, timeouts and paging.
A `Promise<void>` settling after value-channel clearing.
clearAll: Clears every data channel owned by the concrete store, including record and byte channels when present.
clearAll.ctx: Optional caller-authored `IOperationContext`: `signal` is an object with boolean `aborted` and callable `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`; `timeoutMs` is a nonnegative safe integer including 0; `pageSize` is an integer from 1 to 4096. `orgId` is an optional canonical lowercase UUID, including the zero UUID. Each field defaults to `undefined`. Concrete backends execute cancellation, timeouts and paging.
A `Promise<void>` for the concrete backend’s full clear operation.
dispose: Release accepted work and original native resources without acquiring any new close authority.
The original cached main cleanup Promise; native cleanup failure rejects with its original reachable cause.
sync: Optional synchronous string channel supplied only by synchronous backends; asynchronous stores expose undefined.
Absent when the backend does not provide synchronous access.
[Symbol.asyncDispose]: Use the original asynchronous resource-disposal protocol after accepted work drains.
The separately cached symbolic Promise reports cleanup failure and resolves, without replacing the main cleanup Promise.
